q: Which club plays its home games at Anfield?
sub: Liverpool have played there since the club was founded in 1892.
note: Ground confirmed. Two problems with the old sub: Wikipedia has the 1892 split as a dispute over how the club was run and over buying the land, not a rent row, and it handed over the answer to the hard Everton at Anfield row later in this file. Replaced with a clean line.

q: Which club plays its home games at Old Trafford?
sub: The ground opened on 19 February 1910, and Liverpool won the first match 4-3.
note: Confirmed: first game 19 February 1910, Liverpool won 4-3.

q: Which club plays its home games at Stamford Bridge?
sub: The ground opened in 1877 for the London Athletic Club, and the club was founded later to fill it.
note: Confirmed: opened 1877 for the London Athletic Club, and the Mears brothers founded Chelsea to occupy it.

q: Which club played its home games at the Etihad Stadium in 2024-25?
sub: They moved in during the summer of 2003.
note: Club confirmed. A sponsored ground name is a live fact, so the present tense is anchored to a named season.

q: Which club plays its home games at St James' Park?
sub: Football has been played on the site since 1880.
note: Confirmed: City moved from Maine Road in the summer of 2003.

q: Which club plays its home games at Villa Park?
sub: The first match there was a friendly against Blackburn Rovers in April 1897.
note: Confirmed: Newcastle Rangers played on the site in 1880.

q: Which club played at Goodison Park until 2025?
sub: The last men's match there was a 2-0 win over Southampton on 18 May 2025.
note: Confirmed: friendly against Blackburn Rovers on 17 April 1897.

q: Which club plays its home games at Molineux?
sub: Named after Benjamin Molineux, who bought the land in 1744.
note: Confirmed: the men's team's last game there was a 2-0 win over Southampton on 18 May 2025, Ndiaye scoring both. Already anchored to a year, so it survives the live-fact test.

q: Which club plays its home games at Craven Cottage, on the bank of the Thames?
sub: The Cottage itself is a pavilion in the corner, built in 1905.
note: Confirmed: Benjamin Molineux bought the land in 1744 and built Molineux House on it.

q: Which south London club plays its home games at Selhurst Park?
sub: The ground opened in August 1924 and they lost the first game there 1-0.
note: Confirmed: the Cottage Pavilion dates from 1905, and the Riverside Stand backs onto the Thames.

q: Which club played its home games at the King Power Stadium in 2024-25?
sub: Gary Lineker performed the opening ceremony in July 2002.
note: Club confirmed, and Gary Lineker did open the ground on 23 July 2002. Sponsored name anchored to a season.

q: Which ground did Arsenal leave in 2006 when they moved to the Emirates Stadium?
sub: Officially Arsenal Stadium, home from 1913 after the club moved north from Plumstead.
note: Confirmed: Arsenal Stadium, home from 6 September 1913 after the move from the Manor Ground in Plumstead to 7 May 2006.

q: Which ground did Tottenham Hotspur leave in 2017?
sub: Their home for 118 years, from 1899.
note: Confirmed: Tottenham's home from 1899 to 2017.

q: Which club moved into the London Stadium, built for the 2012 Olympics, in 2016?
sub: They signed a 99-year lease on the place in March 2013.
note: Confirmed: the 99-year lease was signed on 22 March 2013 and they moved in for 2016-17.

q: Which ground did Sunderland move into in 1997?
sub: Built on the site of Wearmouth Colliery, and named for the miners' Davy lamps.
note: Confirmed: opened 30 July 1997 on the Wearmouth Colliery site, the name taken from the miners' Davy lamps. Kept as the easy end of the 1997 move, which is why the Roker Park row goes.

q: What is the famous home end at Anfield called?
sub: Named by a local journalist after a Boer War hill where British troops died.
note: Confirmed: Ernest Edwards of the Liverpool Echo named it after the Boer War hill where a local regiment took heavy losses.

q: Which end at Old Trafford traditionally holds Manchester United's loudest support?
sub: It was the last stand at the ground to be given a roof, and the last to be seated.
note: Confirmed: the Stretford End was the last stand to be covered and the last to be seated.

q: Which club has a cannon on its crest?
sub: From the Royal Arsenal armaments works in Woolwich, where the club started in 1886.
note: Confirmed: the 1888 crest carried cannons from the Woolwich borough arms, and the munitions workers formed the club in October 1886.

q: Which club has a liver bird on its crest?
sub: The city's symbol. It flew on a flag over Anfield as early as September 1892.
note: Confirmed almost word for word: the liver bird first appeared on a flag over Anfield in September 1892, two weeks after the club's first competitive match.

q: Which colour shirts do Leeds United wear at home?
sub: Don Revie switched them to all white in 1961-62 to look like Real Madrid.
note: Confirmed: Revie switched to an all-white strip in the style of Real Madrid in 1961-62. Kept as the easy end of this fact, so the Don Revie row in hard is dropped as its mirror.

q: Which ground did Manchester City leave in 2003?
sub: Their home for 80 years, from 1923.
note: Confirmed: City's home from 1923 to 2003.

q: Which ground did Southampton leave in 2001 when they moved to St Mary's Stadium?
sub: The site is now a housing estate with blocks named after old Saints players.
note: Confirmed: the site is now housing, with Le Tissier Court, Ted Bates Court and Channon Court among the blocks.

q: Which ground did West Ham United leave in 2016?
a: The Boleyn Ground, also known as Upton Park
sub: Boleyn because a nearby house was called Boleyn Castle, after Anne Boleyn.
note: Confirmed: Green Street House was known locally as Boleyn Castle for its link to Anne Boleyn.

q: Which ground did Leicester City leave in 2002?
sub: Their home for 111 years. The new ground went up 200 yards away.
note: Confirmed: 111 years of football, and the new site was 200 yards south.

q: Which ground did Sunderland leave in 1997?
sub: It hosted four matches at the 1966 World Cup.
note: Drop as an internal mirror. The easy row asks which ground Sunderland moved into in 1997 and this one asks which they left in 1997, the same move read from both ends, so the two kill each other. The facts hold up, including the four 1966 World Cup games at Roker Park.

q: What was the King Power Stadium called when it opened in 2002?
sub: The crisp firm had a ten-year naming deal. King Power took over in July 2011.
note: Confirmed: Walkers signed a ten-year naming deal in 2002 and King Power took the rights on 5 July 2011.

q: What was the Etihad Stadium called before the 2011 sponsorship deal?
sub: Also known as Eastlands while it was being built.
note: Confirmed, Eastlands included. Already anchored to the 2011 deal.

q: Which sporting event was Manchester City's Etihad Stadium originally built for?
sub: It held 38,000 for the Games, with a running track that was later dug out.
note: Confirmed: built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games, 38,000 for the Games, and the track was lifted and relaid elsewhere.

q: Which club played its home games at the bet365 Stadium in 2024-25?
sub: They moved in during 1997, onto the site of the old Stafford No.2 Colliery.
note: Club confirmed and the sponsored name is anchored to a season. Sub corrected: Wikipedia has the ground built on the former Stafford No.2 Colliery, closed in 1969, not on a site at Trentham Lakes.

q: What was the bet365 Stadium called before it was renamed in 2016?
sub: It opened on 30 August 1997, named after a building society.
note: Confirmed: opened 30 August 1997 under a £1 million ten-year deal with the Britannia Building Society, renamed bet365 Stadium on 1 June 2016.

q: Which club plays its home games at The Hawthorns?
sub: It was the sixth ground the club had used when they moved in, in 1900.
note: Confirmed: the sixth ground the club used, from 1900.

q: Which club plays its home games at Ewood Park?
sub: Jack Walker's steel fortune paid for the rebuild in the early 1990s.
note: Confirmed: Walker sold Walkersteel for £330 million and rebuilt three stands from 1992.

q: Which club plays its home games at Carrow Road?
sub: The whole ground was put up in 82 days in 1935.
note: Confirmed: 82 days, opened 31 August 1935.

q: Which club plays its home games at Fratton Park?
sub: Red socks from 1947-48, added as a memorial to soldiers lost in wartime.
note: Ground confirmed. This one looked like folklore and is not: Wikipedia records the red socks as a memorial to soldiers lost in wartime, red being the British Army colour, following a suggestion by Montgomery, from 1947-48. Sub tightened to exactly that.

q: Which club plays its home games at the Riverside Stadium?
sub: It opened in August 1995.
note: Confirmed: first game 26 August 1995.

q: Which club plays its home games at Kenilworth Road?
sub: Their home since 1905, and the away end is reached through a row of terraced houses.
note: Confirmed: Luton's home since 1905, and the Oak Road End is entered through the row of houses.

q: Which club plays its home games at Vicarage Road?
sub: Saracens rugby club shared it from 1997 to 2013.
note: Confirmed: Saracens were there from 1997 until February 2013.

q: What is Chelsea's traditional home end at Stamford Bridge called?
sub: Supporters nicknamed the 1930 south terrace the Shed and the club adopted it.
note: Confirmed: the 1930 south terrace was the Fulham Road End until supporters renamed it the Shed.

q: Which end at St James' Park is named after the city's old gallows?
sub: At the other end is the Leazes End, named after Leazes Park.
note: Confirmed: Gallowgate for the old city gallows, Leazes End for Leazes Park.

q: Which end at Villa Park is named after a former owner of Aston Hall?
sub: Sir Thomas Holte. The pitch itself covers the Dovehouse Pool, an ornamental pond.
note: Naming confirmed. Sub corrected: the kitchen garden was part of the wider Lower Grounds, while the pitch sits on the filled-in Dovehouse Pool.

q: Which club has a cockerel standing on a ball on its crest?
sub: Harry Hotspur dug in his spurs, and spurs belong on a fighting cock.
note: Crest confirmed, cockerel on a football from 1909, Hotspur's spurs and the fighting cock link included. Pulled to easy: the Arsenal cannon and the liver bird are both easy in this file and this is no harder.

q: Which bird sits on a football on the Norwich City crest?
sub: City first turned out in yellow with green collars and cuffs in 1907-08.
note: Crest confirmed as a canary resting on a football. The chairman who bred canaries is only one of two accounts Wikipedia carries, the other being John Bowman's 1905 interview, so that origin claim is out and the sub now carries the documented kit change. Pulled to easy: anyone who has heard Norwich called the Canaries answers instantly.

q: Which club switched to red shirts in 1902, when it stopped being called Newton Heath?
sub: Newton Heath had worn white shirts with navy blue shorts since 1896.
note: Confirmed: red shirts, white shorts and black socks from the 1902 name change. Sub corrected, the white with blue cord line is not what the source says.

q: Which Liverpool manager put the team in an all-red kit in 1964?
sub: Red for danger, red for power. Before that it was red shirts and white shorts.
note: Confirmed: Shankly changed to an all-red strip in 1964, red for danger and red for power.

q: Which electronics company's name was on Manchester United's shirts from 1983 to 2000?
sub: One of the longest and richest shirt deals in English football, seventeen years of it.
note: Sharp confirmed, but Wikipedia dates the deal 1983 to 2000, not 1982, so the question now matches the source. The Vodafone line is gone: nothing I could reach documents the 2000-01 handover, and this row was flagged conf likely for exactly that reason.

q: Which club did Arsenal beat 4-2 in the last match at Highbury in May 2006?
sub: The win took fourth place off Tottenham on the final day.
note: Confirmed: Arsenal 4 Wigan Athletic 2 on 7 May 2006, and the result kept fourth place ahead of Tottenham.

q: Who scored a hat-trick in Arsenal's final match at Highbury in 2006?
sub: He kissed the turf afterwards.
note: Confirmed: Henry's hat-trick, and he kissed the turf after the last goal ever scored at the ground.

q: What was built on the site of Highbury after Arsenal left?
a: Flats, in a development called Highbury Square
sub: 711 apartments. The listed Art Deco East Stand front was kept, and the pitch is a garden.
note: Confirmed: 711 properties, the listed stand fronts kept, the pitch now a communal garden.

q: Which club beat Manchester City 1-0 in the last match at Maine Road in May 2003?
sub: Michael Svensson scored the ground's last goal.
note: Confirmed: 11 May 2003, City lost 1-0 and Michael Svensson scored the ground's last goal.

q: Which Southampton player scored the last competitive goal at The Dell?
sub: A volley in the closing minutes of the last league game there, 3-2 against Arsenal.
note: Confirmed: 19 May 2001, a volley in the final minutes to beat Arsenal 3-2. The source says nothing about him coming off the bench, so that detail is out rather than passed on.

q: Which club did West Ham United beat 3-2 in the final match at the Boleyn Ground?
sub: Winston Reid scored the winner on 10 May 2016.
note: Confirmed: 3-2 on 10 May 2016, Reid's 80th minute goal the winner.

q: Who scored the last goal at White Hart Lane, in May 2017?
sub: A consolation. Tottenham beat Manchester United 2-1 to close the ground.
note: Confirmed: Rooney scored the ground's last goal in a 2-1 home win, so the consolation line is right.

q: Where did Tottenham Hotspur play their home league games in 2017-18?
sub: The new ground was not ready, so they spent a whole season there.
note: Confirmed: announced 28 April 2017 that all 2017-18 home games would be at Wembley.

q: Who scored the first competitive goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, in April 2019?
sub: Crystal Palace were beaten 2-0.
note: Confirmed: Son scored the first official goal at the new ground, 2-0 against Crystal Palace.

q: Which two clubs have groundshared at Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park?
sub: Charlton from 1985 to 1991, Wimbledon from 1991 to 2003.
note: Confirmed: Charlton from 1985 to 1991, Wimbledon from 1991 until the move to Milton Keynes in 2003.

q: Where did Fulham play from 2002 to 2004 while Craven Cottage was being rebuilt?
sub: Two seasons as lodgers at Queens Park Rangers.
note: Confirmed: they decamped to Loftus Road after April 2002 and were back at the Cottage for 2004-05, so two seasons away.

q: Which club played at Anfield before Liverpool existed?
sub: They fell out with landlord John Houlding in 1892, left for Goodison, and he founded Liverpool.
note: Confirmed, Houlding and the 1892 split included. The Anfield easy row's sub used to give this away, and that sub has been changed.

q: Where did Manchester United play home games from 1941 to 1949, after Old Trafford was bombed?
sub: They rented Manchester City's ground for £5,000 a year plus a cut of the gate.
note: Confirmed to the penny: £5,000 a year plus a percentage of the gate.

q: Which stand at Old Trafford was renamed after Sir Alex Ferguson in 2011?
sub: Renamed on 5 November 2011, marking 25 years in the job.
note: Confirmed: renamed the Sir Alex Ferguson Stand on 5 November 2011.

q: Which Chelsea director, killed in a helicopter crash in 1996, has a Stamford Bridge stand named after him?
sub: His money rebuilt the club in the early 1990s.
note: Confirmed, spelling included: Matthew Harding died in a helicopter crash on 22 October 1996.

q: What was Bolton Wanderers' Reebok Stadium renamed in 2014?
sub: Then the University of Bolton Stadium in 2018, then the Toughsheet Community Stadium.
note: Confirmed: Macron branding July 2014, University of Bolton Stadium August 2018, Toughsheet Community Stadium 1 July 2023.

q: At 551 feet above sea level, which ground was the highest of the 92 English league grounds in 2024-25?
sub: That is 168 metres above sea level.
note: Figure confirmed, and the source puts it as the highest of all Premier League and Football League clubs. The old wording claimed the highest ever used by any English league club, an open-ended superlative over a set of clubs that changes every year, so it is anchored to a season.

q: Which ground did Stoke City leave in 1997, after 119 years?
sub: It was the oldest ground in the Football League when it was pulled down.
note: Confirmed: 119 years, and the oldest operational ground in the Football League when it came down.

q: Which ground did Derby County leave in 1997 for Pride Park?
sub: Francis Ley built it for baseball for his foundry workers, hence the name.
note: Confirmed: Sir Francis Ley built it for his foundry workers and it was first called Ley's Baseball Ground.

q: Which ground was the first in England to have permanent floodlights, installed in 1950?
sub: The first game under them was against Bournemouth on 31 October 1950.
note: Confirmed: the first ground in England to have permanent floodlighting, 1950, first game 31 October 1950 against Bournemouth and Boscombe Athletic.

q: Which club adopted red and blue striped shirts in 1973, inspired by Barcelona?
sub: Malcolm Allison's overhaul. Before that they played in claret and blue.
note: Confirmed: Allison arrived in 1973 and took the red and blue vertical stripes from Barcelona, after claret and blue.

q: Which club has a song thrush perched on a hawthorn branch on its crest?
sub: A throstle is a song thrush, and the branch came in after they moved to The Hawthorns.
note: Confirmed: a throstle on a hawthorn branch, the branch replacing a crossbar after the 1900 move.

q: Which manager put Leeds United in an all-white kit, copying Real Madrid?
sub: From 1961-62. Before that they had worn blue and gold.
note: Facts are right, 1961-62 and Real Madrid. Dropped as the mirror of the easy Leeds row, whose sub already states Revie and Real Madrid outright, so the two cannot both ship. The easy end is what this deck is short of, so the one-pointer stays and this goes.

q: Which company's name was on Liverpool's shirts when they won the 2019-20 Premier League?
sub: The bank took over from Carlsberg, who had been there from 1992 to 2010.
note: Confirmed: Standard Chartered took over at the start of 2010-11 after Carlsberg from 1992, so they were on the shirt in 2019-20.

q: Which ground hosted a 1966 World Cup semi-final, the only one ever played at an English club ground?
sub: West Germany beat the Soviet Union 2-1 there on 25 July 1966.
note: Confirmed: West Germany 2-1 Soviet Union on 25 July 1966, and the source states Goodison is the only English club ground to have staged a World Cup semi-final.

q: In February 2018 a Premier League crowd of 83,222 at Wembley set a record. Which two clubs played?
sub: Spurs won 1-0 during their season away from home.
note: Confirmed: Tottenham 1-0 Arsenal at Wembley on 10 February 2018. Rephrased so the record is an event that happened in 2018 rather than a standing claim about today.

q: In January 1993 just 3,039 saw a Premier League game at Selhurst Park, a record low at the time. Which club were at home?
sub: They lost 3-1 to Everton, and their 8,353 average that season was a league low too.
note: Confirmed: Wimbledon 1-3 Everton on 26 January 1993, and 8,353 is the lowest season average in the records list. Record claim anchored to the time. The low crowd has to stay in the question, otherwise Crystal Palace is a defensible answer for a game at Selhurst Park.

q: Which Leicester City player scored the last goal at Filbert Street, in May 2002?
sub: Leicester beat Tottenham 2-1 to close the ground.
note: Confirmed: Piper scored the ground's last goal in a 2-1 win over Tottenham on 12 May 2002.

q: Which club did Middlesbrough beat 2-0 in the first match at the Riverside Stadium in 1995?
sub: Craig Hignett and Jan Aage Fjortoft scored.
note: Confirmed: 26 August 1995, 2-0, Hignett then Fjortoft.

q: Which old ground's gates were re-erected outside Middlesbrough's Riverside Stadium in 2005?
sub: The same gates that were locked when the club went into liquidation in 1986.
note: Confirmed: the gates locked at the 1986 liquidation were put up outside the Riverside in 2005.

q: Which Dutch club played Sunderland in the first match at the Stadium of Light in 1997?
sub: A 0-0 friendly, after Prince Andrew opened the ground.
note: Confirmed: a 0-0 friendly against Ajax on 30 July 1997, Prince Andrew opening the ground.

q: Which ground averaged 75,821 spectators in 2006-07, a Premier League record at the time?
sub: It was also the biggest ground in the league that season.
note: Figure, ground and season confirmed from the records list. Superlative anchored to the season instead of left standing in the present.

q: Which club were the visitors for Arsenal's first competitive match at the Emirates Stadium, in 2006?
sub: Gilberto Silva scored Arsenal's first competitive goal at the ground.
note: Confirmed. Worth a reader's aside: Villa's Olof Mellberg scored the ground's first competitive goal, Gilberto Silva the first for Arsenal.

q: What was the Emirates Stadium site known as before the naming deal was signed?
sub: Emirates signed a 15-year deal in 2004 worth around £100 million.
note: Confirmed: Ashburton Grove, and Emirates took 15-year naming rights in 2004 in a deal estimated at £100 million.

q: Which ground was called the Sports Direct Arena between 2011 and 2012?
sub: Newcastle dropped it after a year when Wonga bought the naming rights and gave the name back.
note: Confirmed: renamed on 10 November 2011, and Wonga bought the rights on 9 October 2012 and restored the old name.

q: Which Norwich City ground was given up after part of the pitch sank into old chalk workings?
sub: One corner dropped as much as 30 feet. Carrow Road replaced it in 1935.
note: Confirmed: one corner of the pitch subsided up to 30 feet after old chalk workings collapsed, and Carrow Road opened on 31 August 1935.

q: Which stand at Elland Road was the largest cantilever stand in the world when it was finished in 1993?
sub: It cost £5.5 million.
note: Confirmed: largest cantilever stand in the world on completion, 17,000 seats, £5.5 million.

q: Which Everton stand was renamed after Howard Kendall in 2016?
sub: It became the Howard Kendall Gwladys Street End that July.
note: Confirmed: renamed the Howard Kendall Gwladys Street End in July 2016.

q: What colour shirts were Everton wearing when they moved into Goodison Park in 1892?
a: Salmon pink and dark blue stripes
sub: Royal blue only arrived in 1901-02. They had also tried black with a scarlet sash.
note: Confirmed: salmon pink and dark blue stripes on the 1892 move, royal blue first used in 1901-02, and the black shirt with a scarlet sash earlier.

q: Which county cricket club played first-class matches at Sheffield United's Bramall Lane until 1973?
sub: The ground opened for cricket in 1855, and Yorkshire played 391 first-class matches there.
note: Confirmed: Yorkshire's last match there was in August 1973. The 391 is Yorkshire's own tally between 1863 and 1973, not the ground's total since 1855, so the sub now says whose it is. Pulled from extreme to normal: Bramall Lane is in Sheffield, so the county answers itself and a ten-pointer it is not.

q: The cockerel on the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is a replica, dents and all. Which player shot the original with an air rifle?
sub: The original bronze cockerel was made by a former player and went up in 1910.
note: The air rifle is documented: the source calls the stadium bird a faithful replica of the original including the dents Gascoigne made shooting at it. The 4.5 metre fibreglass and the South Stand are not in what I could read, so the sub drops them for the 1910 bronze original by former player William James Scott.

q: Manchester United changed out of their grey kit at half time in 1996, claiming they could not pick each other out. Who were they playing?
sub: The kit was binned after five games. They never won a competitive match in it.
note: Confirmed: dropped after five games, changed at half time against Southampton, and United never won a competitive game in it in five attempts.

q: Derby County's first competitive match at Pride Park, in August 1997, was abandoned. What went wrong?
sub: They went out eleven minutes into the second half against Wimbledon.
note: Confirmed: 13 August 1997 against Wimbledon, Derby 2-1 up, the lights went out in the 11th minute of the second half and Uriah Rennie abandoned it after half an hour of failed generators.

q: Which club wore the Acorns Children's Hospice logo on their shirts, for nothing, in 2008-09 and 2009-10?
sub: The first deal of its kind in the Premier League. Acorns stayed on as charity partner.
note: Confirmed: Villa gave the shirt to Acorns for 2008-09 and 2009-10, the first deal of its kind in Premier League history, and Acorns stayed on as charity partner.

q: Griffin Park, Brentford's old ground, was the only English league ground with one of what on each of its four corners?
sub: The Griffin, the Princess Royal, the New Inn and the Brook.
note: Confirmed: the only football ground in England with a pub on each corner, the Griffin, the Princess Royal, the New Inn and the Brook.
